questions.question: The Aravalli Range, counted among the oldest fold mountain systems in the world, primarily stretches across which Indian state?
questions.explanation: The Aravalli Range runs primarily through Rajasthan (roughly northeast to southwest across the state), extending marginally into Haryana, Delhi and Gujarat. It is one of the oldest fold mountains, formed in the Precambrian era.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws to every person?
questions.explanation: Article 14 guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws to all persons, including foreigners. Article 15 prohibits discrimination, Article 17 abolishes untouchability, and Article 19 deals with freedom of speech and other freedoms.

questions.question: Who founded the Arya Samaj in Bombay in 1875 with the motto 'Back to the Vedas'?
questions.explanation: Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in 1875 in Bombay, urging a return to the authority of the Vedas. Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj (Atmiya Sabha), and Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission.

questions.question: Sattriya, recognised as one of the eight classical dance forms of India, traces its origin to the monasteries (satras) established by the saint Srimanta Sankardeva in which state?
questions.explanation: Sattriya was created by the 15th-16th century Vaishnavite saint Srimanta Sankardeva and was preserved for centuries in the satras (monasteries) of Assam, performed traditionally by celibate monks called bhokots.

questions.question: Chisel : Sculptor :: Needle : ?
questions.explanation: A chisel is the primary working tool of a sculptor, just as a needle is the primary working tool of a tailor. The other options are materials, actions or machines, not the person who wields the tool.

questions.question: In a certain code language, DELHI is written as IHLED. Following the same rule, how is MUMBAI written in that code?
questions.explanation: The code simply reverses the word: DELHI written backwards is IHLED. Reversing MUMBAI gives IABMUM.

questions.question: Three of the following four words are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd one out.
questions.explanation: Square, Triangle, and Circle are two-dimensional shapes. Cube is a three-dimensional shape, making it the odd one out.

questions.question: At the Paris 2024 Olympic Games, which Indian shooter created history by winning two bronze medals, becoming the first Indian since Independence to win two medals at a single Olympic Games?
questions.explanation: Manu Bhaker won bronze in the women's 10m air pistol and then another bronze in the 10m air pistol mixed team event (with Sarabjot Singh) at Paris 2024, becoming the first Indian since Independence to win two medals at one Olympics.

questions.question: The 2025 Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Heads of State Summit, the largest in the grouping's history, was held from 31 August to 1 September 2025 in which Chinese city?
questions.explanation: The 25th Meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of State was hosted by China in Tianjin from 31 August to 1 September 2025, where leaders adopted the Tianjin Declaration. Qingdao had hosted the 2018 SCO summit.

questions.question: In November 2024, DRDO successfully flight-tested the nuclear-capable K-4 submarine-launched ballistic missile for the first time from which Indian submarine?
questions.explanation: The K-4 SLBM (with a reported range of around 3,500 km) was flight-tested for the first time from a submarine, INS Arighaat, in the Bay of Bengal in November 2024. INS Arighaat had been commissioned in August 2024.

questions.question: Find the simple interest on ₹8,000 at 6% per annum for a period of 9 months.
questions.explanation: 9 months = 0.75 years. SI = (8000 × 6 × 0.75)/100 = 8000 × 4.5/100 = ₹360. (₹480 would be the interest for a full year.)

questions.question: The average of five consecutive even numbers is 26. What is the largest of these numbers?
questions.explanation: For consecutive even numbers the average equals the middle number, so the numbers are 22, 24, 26, 28, 30. The largest is 30.

questions.question: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon measures 24°. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.explanation: The exterior angles of any polygon sum to 360°. For a regular polygon with n sides, each exterior angle = 360/n, so n = 360/24 = 15.

questions.question: A number is increased by 20% and the resulting number is then decreased by 20%. If the final value is 480, what was the original number?
questions.explanation: Net change = 1.2 × 0.8 = 0.96, i.e., a 4% decrease. So 0.96x = 480, giving x = 480/0.96 = 500.

questions.question: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 12:40?
questions.explanation: At 12:40, the minute hand is at the 8 mark = 240° from 12. The hour hand has moved 40 × 0.5° = 20° from 12. The angle between them is 240 − 20 = 220°, so the smaller angle is 360 − 220 = 140°.

questions.question: Prolonged deficiency of which vitamin causes scurvy, a disease marked by bleeding gums and slow wound healing?
questions.explanation: Scurvy results from deficiency of vitamin C (ascorbic acid), which is essential for collagen synthesis. Citrus fruits and amla are rich sources. (Vitamin K deficiency affects clotting; B12 deficiency causes anaemia.)

questions.question: Which of the following is the SI unit of electric current?
questions.explanation: The ampere (A) is the SI base unit of electric current. Volt measures potential difference, ohm measures resistance and watt measures power.

questions.question: A metrorail accident victim with severe blood loss needs an urgent transfusion, but her blood group cannot be determined immediately. Which blood group can be safely given to a person of any blood group in such emergencies?
questions.explanation: O negative red cells carry neither A/B antigens nor the Rh(D) antigen, so they are not attacked by any recipient's antibodies — which is why O negative is called the 'universal donor' group. AB positive is the universal recipient.

questions.question: The 18th Pravasi Bharatiya Divas Convention, held in January 2025 to mark the contribution of the Indian diaspora, was hosted by which city?
questions.explanation: The 18th Pravasi Bharatiya Divas Convention was held in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, from 8-10 January 2025, coinciding with the 108th birth anniversary of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose.

questions.question: NITI Aayog, set up by the Government of India in January 2015 as a policy think-tank, replaced which earlier institution?
questions.explanation: The Planning Commission, created in 1950, which formulated the Five-Year Plans, was replaced by NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) on 1 January 2015, shifting from centralised planning to cooperative federalism.

questions.question: A chain of shallow reefs and low islands divides the Bay of Bengal from the Gulf of Mannar between India and Sri Lanka. Which strait, named after a British officer, connects these two water bodies?
questions.explanation: The Palk Strait, named after Robert Palk, a Governor of Madras, separates Tamil Nadu from northern Sri Lanka, and the Gulf of Mannar lies to its south, with Adam's Bridge (Rama Setu) reef chain between them. The named channels listed as distractors lie in the Lakshadweep/Andaman region.

questions.question: India's Aditya-L1 mission, launched by ISRO in September 2023, is designed to study which aspect of the Sun?
options: B) Solar corona and solar winds
questions.explanation: Aditya-L1 is India's first dedicated solar mission, positioned at the L1 Lagrange point between Earth and the Sun. It studies the solar corona, solar winds, and coronal mass ejections.

questions.question: Find the next term in the series: 3, 7, 16, 35, 74, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 4, 9, 19, 39, and each difference equals twice the previous difference plus 1 (4→9→19→39→79). So the next term is 74 + 79 = 153.

questions.question: A is B's brother. C is A's mother. D is C's father. How is A related to D?
questions.explanation: C is the mother of both A and B. D is C's father, so D is the grandfather of A. Therefore A (a male, being B's brother) is D's grandson.

questions.question: In a certain code, each word is replaced by the sum of the positions of its letters in the English alphabet. If 'PEN' is coded as 35 (P=16, E=5, N=14), what is the code for 'CAP'?
A mobile cover retailer marks his stock 60% above cost price but clears old designs with a flat discount of 25% on the marked price. What is his profit percentage on such sales?
questions.explanation: Take CP = ₹100. Marked price = ₹160. Selling price = 160 × 0.75 = ₹120. Profit = ₹20 on ₹100, i.e., 20%.

questions.question: At what rate of interest per annum, compounded annually, will ₹12,500 amount to ₹14,580 in 2 years?
A and B together can complete a report in 12 days, B and C together in 15 days, and C and A together in 20 days. In how many days can all three working together complete the report?
questions.explanation: 1/A + 1/B = 1/12, 1/B + 1/C = 1/15, 1/C + 1/A = 1/20. Adding: 2(1/A + 1/B + 1/C) = 1/12 + 1/15 + 1/20 = (5 + 4 + 3)/60 = 1/5. So the combined one-day work = 1/10, meaning all three take 10 days.

questions.question:
The table below shows the number of electric vehicles registered in a state over three years (in thousands).

Year | Cars | Two-wheelers
2022 | 40   | 160
2023 | 64   | 210
2024 | 96   | 260

Over the three years combined, two-wheeler registrations formed approximately what percentage of total EV registrations in the state?
questions.explanation: Two-wheelers: 160 + 210 + 260 = 630 thousand. Total registrations: (40+160) + (64+210) + (96+260) = 200 + 274 + 356 = 830 thousand. Percentage = 630/830 × 100 ≈ 75.9%.

questions.question:
The table below shows the number of electric cars registered in a state over three years (in thousands).

Year | Cars registered
2022 | 40
2023 | 64
2024 | 96

In which year was the percentage increase in car registrations over the previous year the highest?
options: C) The increase was equal in both years
questions.explanation: In 2023 the increase was (64 − 40)/40 = 60%. In 2024 it was (96 − 64)/64 = 50%. So the percentage increase was highest in 2023.

questions.question: If x = 2 + √3, what is the value of x + 1/x?

Statements: All novels are books. Some books are classics.
Conclusions: I. Some novels are classics. II. Some books are novels.
Decide which conclusion(s) logically follow.
options: C) Both conclusions I and II follow
D) Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: Conclusion II follows directly from 'All novels are books' (if all novels are books, then some books must be novels). Conclusion I does not necessarily follow: the classics may all be non-novel books, so no overlap between novels and classics is guaranteed.

questions.question: Five friends A, B, C, D and E sit in a row facing north. C sits in the middle. B sits to the immediate right of C. A sits at one of the extreme ends, and E does not sit at any extreme end. Who sits second from the left end?
questions.explanation: Place positions 1-5 from left. C is at 3 and B at 4. E is not at an end and the only middle-adjacent seat left free of constraints... if A takes end 1, then E must take 2 (D gets 5); if A takes end 5, D takes 1 and E still takes 2. Either way, position 2 — second from the left — is E.

questions.question: If 1 March 2025 falls on a Saturday, on what day of the week does 30 May 2025 fall?
questions.explanation: From 1 March to 30 May, the number of days elapsed = 30 (rest of March) + 30 (April) + 30 (up to 30 May) = 90 days. 90 ÷ 7 leaves remainder 6. Saturday + 6 days = Friday.

questions.question: Baking soda, commonly used in kitchens as a leavening agent and as a mild antacid, is chemically known as:
questions.explanation: Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃). Sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃) is washing soda, and sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is caustic soda.

questions.question: Sound needs a material medium to propagate, because it travels as a mechanical vibration of particles. In which of the following will a ringing bell produce no sound at all?
questions.explanation: Sound waves are mechanical waves requiring a medium of particles. In a vacuum there are no particles to vibrate, so the vibrations cannot travel — the bell's motion produces no sound. Sound actually travels fastest in solids like steel.

questions.question: Pure water at 25°C is neither acidic nor basic. What is the pH of such a neutral solution?
questions.explanation: On the pH scale of 0 to 14, a value of 7 (the pH of pure water at 25°C) is neutral; values below 7 are acidic and above 7 are basic.

questions.question: At the Paris 2024 Olympic Games, the Indian men's hockey team repeated its podium finish from Tokyo 2020 by winning which medal?
questions.explanation: India's men's hockey team beat Spain 2-1 to win the bronze medal at Paris 2024, its second consecutive Olympic bronze after Tokyo 2020, where it had ended a 41-year medal drought.

questions.question: If a + b + c = 0, then what is the value of a³ + b³ + c³?
questions.explanation: Using the identity a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca): when a + b + c = 0, the right side is 0, so a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.

questions.question: An electric car of mass 800 kg accelerates uniformly from rest to a speed of 20 m/s in 5 seconds. What is the average force exerted on the car during this acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration a = (20 − 0)/5 = 4 m/s². Force F = ma = 800 × 4 = 3,200 N.

questions.question: Under which Governor-General of India was the Subsidiary Alliance system — by which princely states accepted British troops and a Resident in exchange for 'protection' — first systematically introduced?
questions.explanation: Lord Wellesley (Governor-General 1798-1805) introduced the Subsidiary Alliance, first imposed on Hyderabad (1798) and then Mysore, Awadh and others. Dalhousie later devised the Doctrine of Lapse, and Cornwallis is known for the Permanent Settlement.

questions.question: In the Bihar Legislative Assembly election whose results were declared in November 2025, the National Democratic Alliance won a sweeping majority. How many of the 243 assembly seats did the NDA secure?
questions.explanation: The NDA won 202 of the 243 seats in the November 2025 Bihar election (BJP 89, JD(U) 85, LJP(RV) 19 among others), while the Mahagathbandhan was reduced to 35 seats.

questions.question: Find the next term in the series: 2, 3, 8, 27, 112, ?
questions.explanation: The pattern multiplies by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 successively and adds the same number: 2×1+1 = 3, 3×2+2 = 8, 8×3+3 = 27, 27×4+4 = 112, 112×5+5 = 565.

questions.question: The average of 11 test scores is 50. The average of the first six scores is 49 and the average of the last six scores is 52. What is the sixth score?
questions.explanation: First six sum = 6 × 49 = 294; last six sum = 6 × 52 = 312; total of eleven = 11 × 50 = 550. The sixth score is counted in both groups, so it equals 294 + 312 − 550 = 56.

questions.question: Find the smallest positive number which, when divided by 5, leaves remainder 2; when divided by 6, leaves remainder 3; and when divided by 7, leaves remainder 4.
questions.explanation: In each case the remainder is 3 less than the divisor (2 = 5−3, 3 = 6−3, 4 = 7−3), so the number is of the form LCM(5, 6, 7)·k − 3 = 210k − 3. The smallest positive value is 210 − 3 = 207. Check: 207 = 41×5 + 2, 207 = 34×6 + 3, 207 = 29×7 + 4.

questions.question: A baker sells item A at a 20% profit and item B at a 10% loss. The cost prices of A and B are in the ratio 3 : 2, and their combined cost price is ₹2,500. What is the baker's overall profit or loss percentage on the two items together?
questions.explanation: Cost prices: A = ₹1,500 and B = ₹1,000 (ratio 3:2). Profit on A = 20% of 1,500 = ₹300; loss on B = 10% of 1,000 = ₹100. Net gain = ₹200 on ₹2,500, i.e., 200/2500 × 100 = 8% profit.

questions.question: A solid metallic cone of radius 12 cm and height 6 cm is completely melted and recast into a solid sphere. What is the radius of the sphere?
questions.explanation: Volume of cone = (1/3)π × 12² × 6 = 288π cm³. For the sphere, (4/3)πr³ = 288π, so r³ = 216 and r = 6 cm.

questions.question:
Four subject tests — Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics and Biology — are held on four consecutive days, Monday to Thursday, with exactly one test per day. The following conditions apply:
(i) Physics is not held on Monday.
(ii) Chemistry is held on the day immediately after Mathematics.
(iii) Biology is held on Wednesday.
(iv) Mathematics is not held on Thursday.
Which subject's test is held on Tuesday?
questions.explanation: Biology is fixed on Wednesday. Chemistry must fall on the day right after Mathematics, so the Maths-Chemistry pair must fit the remaining days (Mon, Tue, Thu). The only consecutive available pair is Mon-Tue: Mathematics on Monday, Chemistry on Tuesday. Mathematics on Thursday would push Chemistry to Friday (impossible), and Tuesday is taken by Biology. Physics then takes Thursday, satisfying condition (i). So Chemistry is held on Tuesday.

questions.question:
Four professionals — A, B, C and D — each practise a different profession (Teacher, Doctor, Engineer, Lawyer) and each lives in a different city (Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata). The following facts are known:
(i) A is not the Doctor and does not live in Delhi.
(ii) The Teacher lives in Kolkata.
(iii) B lives in Chennai and is not the Teacher.
(iv) C is the Engineer.
(v) D is the Lawyer.
Who lives in Kolkata?
questions.explanation: From (iv) and (v), C is the Engineer and D the Lawyer, so A and B must be the Teacher and the Doctor. Since B is not the Teacher, B is the Doctor and A is the Teacher. By (ii) the Teacher lives in Kolkata, so A lives in Kolkata — consistent with (i), since A does not live in Delhi. (B is confirmed in Chennai; C and D occupy Delhi and Mumbai in some order, which the facts leave open.)

questions.question:
Six friends A, B, C, D, E and F sit in a row of six seats numbered 1 to 6 from left to right. The following conditions apply:
(i) B sits on seat 3 (third from the left end).
(ii) A sits between B and F.
(iii) F sits on the seat immediately to the right of A.
(iv) E sits at one of the extreme ends, adjacent to D.
(v) C does not sit adjacent to E.
Who sits on seat 6, the extreme right end?
questions.explanation: From (i)-(iii): B is on 3, A on 4, F on 5. Seats 1, 2 and 6 remain for C, D and E. If E took seat 6, then by (iv) D would have to be on the adjacent seat 5 — occupied by F, impossible. So E takes seat 1, with D adjacent on seat 2. C then takes seat 6, which satisfies (v) since seat 6 is not adjacent to seat 1. Final arrangement: E, D, B, A, F, C — so C sits at the extreme right.
